title.rendered: Rooted and Built Up in Him: The Gospel For Today

excerpt.rendered: You received Christ by grace through faith, and the same way you received Him is the same way you live in Him. Rooted and built up. Not striving and performing. The life of grace is a life of drawing, not straining.

content.rendered:
The Gospel For Today | Monday, May 4, 2026

📖 Today’s Scripture

“So then, just as you received Christ Jesus as Lord, continue to live your lives in him, rooted and built up in him, strengthened in the faith as you were taught, and overflowing with thankfulness.”
Colossians 2:6–7 (NIV) | ESV

📝 Today’s Message

Notice the logic of the verse. You received Christ by faith, not by works, not by performance, not by being good enough. Grace through faith. And the same way you received Him is the same way you continue to live in Him. Rooted and built up, not striving and performing.

A tree does not strain to grow. It draws from its roots. Whatever the weather above ground, drought, storm, wind, the root system keeps drawing from the deep supply. That is the picture of the grace-filled life. You are rooted in Christ. The supply never runs out. The ground never shifts.

Paul prays in Ephesians 3:17–19 that believers would be rooted and established in love, so that they would be able to grasp how wide and long and high and deep is the love of Christ. The depth of your roots in His love is what determines how unshakeable you become when the storms come.

And notice where Paul lands: overflowing with thankfulness. Not straining with effort but overflowing with gratitude. You received Christ freely. Live in Him the same way.

🙏 Prayer

Father, I choose to draw from my roots in You today rather than strain in my own effort. You are my supply, my stability, my ground. I am rooted in Your love, built up in Your grace, strengthened in Your faithfulness. I overflow with thankfulness because I know who holds me. In Jesus’ name. Amen.

🗣️ Declaration

I am rooted and built up in Christ Jesus. The same grace that saved me sustains me, I live by faith, not by striving. My roots go deep into the love of God and I am not moved by what I see above ground. I draw from an inexhaustible supply. I am stable, fruitful and overflowing with thankfulness because I am rooted in Christ.
